assignmentTitle: Fatigue Design of an Automotive Propeller Shaft

criteria.title: Observe the Automotive Drivetrain
criteria.description: Understanding client brief, automotive drivetrain propeller shaft application, and project scope.

criteria.title: Identify Drivetrain Components
criteria.description: Accurate labeling of gearbox flange, universal joints, slip joint spline, shaft tube, differential pinion, and rear wheels on EA-16.

criteria.title: Understand Torque Transmission & Load Path
criteria.description: Tracing torque transmission path from engine gearbox through propeller shaft to differential and road wheels.

criteria.title: Identify Critical Shaft Sections & Stress Concentration
criteria.description: Identifying stress concentration zones at splined joint roots and circumferential weld neck joints.

criteria.title: Analyze Fluctuating Torsional Loading
criteria.description: Calculating mean torque (Tm) and alternating torque (Ta) under fluctuating vehicle load cycles.

criteria.title: Determine Fatigue Strength Factors
criteria.description: Determining surface factor (ka), size factor (kb), reliability factor (kc), and modified shear endurance limit (Sse).

criteria.title: Apply Torsional Fatigue Design Criterion
criteria.description: Applying modified Soderberg fatigue criterion for fluctuating torsional shear stress and FoS calculation.

criteria.title: Propeller Shaft Diameter Verification
criteria.description: Evaluating hollow tubular shaft vs solid shaft construction for mass reduction, polar moment of inertia, and critical speed.

criteria.title: Practical Fatigue Failure & Overload Analysis
criteria.description: Diagnosing 45-degree spiral torsional fatigue cracking, spline fretting wear, and overload failure modes.

criteria.title: Propeller Shaft Fatigue Design Report
criteria.description: Synthesizing comprehensive fatigue design report covering torque calculations, Soderberg criteria, and maintenance guidelines.
